investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T11:18:12–16Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and every downstream contract assertion was left unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with a 409 Conflict because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The error message embedded in the response — "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" — is the earliest violated boundary. Because createAgent() (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first call inside the withCleanup block for all three remote-agent checks, none of the checks can proceed past agent creation, causing a total evidence blackout and cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature group. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is refusing new agent creation requests for the eval service account's organization because the org has reached its swarm agent quota limit of 100. Every eval check in the remote-agents feature group calls POST /api/agents as its first step; when that call returns HTTP 409 with code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100", the runner exits before collecting any evidence, causing all three checks to fail with the same message and leaving the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) entirely unmet. investigations.title: Remote Agent Creation Blocked by Swarm Agent Quota Exhaustion (HTTP 409)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-17T11:18:12–16Z with an identical HTTP 409 response from POST /api/agents, carrying the swarm error "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". Because the failure occurs at the agent creation step shared by all three checks, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and every downstream contract assertion was left unverifiable.
investigations.rootCause: The production swarm backend rejected POST /api/agents with a 409 Conflict because the eval org has reached its remote agent quota limit of 100. The error message embedded in the response — "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" — is the earliest violated boundary. Because createAgent() (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1339) is the first call inside the withCleanup block for all three remote-agent checks, none of the checks can proceed past agent creation, causing a total evidence blackout and cascading failure across the entire remote-agents feature group. This is an eval infrastructure failure against the production API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: SESSION_OPEN_FAILED (404) on Agent Runtime Endpoint in production-api
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval for the production-api runtime environment failed because the agent runtime endpoint returned a 404, causing a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error that terminated the SSE stream immediately after generation_start. As a result, the stream never emitted a generation_completed frame and no image URL was produced, violating both assertions in the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The agent runtime harness backing the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint is unreachable or running an incompatible version in the production-api environment. The stream opened successfully (generation_start was received), but the session establishment call to the agent runtime returned HTTP 404, triggering a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error frame and aborting the generation pipeline before any image artifact could be produced. This is an eval-infrastructure or runtime-configuration failure localized to the production-api agent harness endpoint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so a user-facing outage cannot be confirmed from this data alone.
